title: Prioritized node grooming and maintenance SLAs
creator: Aisha Becker
description: Design and implement an automated 'node grooming' workflow that enforces throughput-backed maintenance SLAs for Dedicated fleets. The goal is to let operations schedule and execute node maintenance (kernel upgrades, driver patches, decommissions) without violating per-customer throughput guarantees. The system will coordinate autoscaler policies, short-term capacity reservations, KV-cache prewarm instructions, and phased traffic reshaping to keep latency and token-throughput SLOs intact. Deliverables: an orchestration controller, a policy DSL for maintenance windows & reservation priorities, a prewarm/rehydration job, and dashboarding/alerts for regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Controller can schedule a maintenance window and allocate throughput reservations for affected customer slices without manual intervention
Autoscaler respects maintenance reservation tokens and avoids scale-downs that would violate the reservation during the window
KV cache prewarm task warms top-10 prefixes for customers with reserved throughput in under 90s and telemetry shows KV hit-rate increases within the window
End-to-end test shows no more than 5% latency p99 increase for reserved customers during a staged drain
Playbook and rollbacks documented; smoke dashboard and on-call alert created
tasks: Spec: define maintenance reservation token semantics, priority levels, and max reservation time
Controller: implement a maintenance coordinator service (API + state machine) to create/inspect/abort maintenance jobs
Autoscaler integration: extend scale-controller to accept reservation tokens and freeze target capacity for specified slices
KV prewarm: add a prewarm task runner that fetches common prefixes and warms remote nodes before traffic cutover
Traffic shaping: implement gradual route weight migration to transfer load away from draining hosts in stages
Test harness: create synthetic workloads to validate throughput guarantees and autoscaler behavior
Dashboard: add per-reservation telemetry (reserved tokens, prewarm success, observed throughput, latency deltas)
Runbook: write maintenance playbook with rollback steps and safety abort thresholds
decisions: Use a lightweight coordinator (Go service) rather than embedding in scheduler to reduce blast radius and allow independent rollouts
Reservation tokens are soft guarantees backed by throttled preemption rather than hard capacity pins to preserve cluster utilization
KV prewarm will be best-effort with success/failure tags; failures will degrade to conservative traffic pacing rather than aborting the maintenance
We will prioritize customer slices by 'reservation priority' (P0..P3) and allow reserving partial throughput percentages rather than full host allocation
Autoscaler freeze window will accept the reservation token and maintain headroom equal to requested throughput converted via the model's measured tokens/sec profile
